The image shows a corn leaf with:
- Numerous small, scattered orange-to-reddish-brown pustules across the leaf surface
- Pustules visible on the leaf blade, densely packed and fairly uniform in size
- The midrib area shows some purple/reddish discoloration
- Pustules appear small, circular to slightly oval
- They appear concentrated and distributed across the upper leaf surface

Key differentiation: The pustules are small, circular, densely packed, and light orange to cinnamon-red in color, appearing predominantly on the upper leaf surface. This matches Southern Rust more closely than Common Rust (which has larger, more elongate, darker reddish-brown pustules on both surfaces). The pustules here are notably small, circular, and densely distributed — hallmark of Southern Rust.
